name: Youth Brigade
label: Dischord
lede: Two Wilson High leftovers, one borrowed van, a record named after a joke in a Dischord ad, and eleven songs that were all D.C. ever got until the band came back thirty years later.

eras.title: What's left after the Teen Idles
eras.text: By late 1980 the first wave of D.C. kid bands had already burned through. The Teen Idles and the Untouchables were done, and Teen Idles singer Nathan Strejcek and Untouchables drummer Danny Ingram, friends from Wilson High, weren't ready to stop.

years.h: Nathan Strejcek and Danny Ingram start Youth Brigade
years.p: With [[The Teen Idles|84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa]] and the [[Untouchables|16d88df0-a2a9-4b3b-87ff-84e90e312d40]] both split, singer [[Nathan Strejcek|b53e7b75-696d-43f5-98ff-bc3d104e0d74]] and drummer [[Danny Ingram|41959411-d1b4-4954-af09-087ac72f69ab]] start a new band. Not to be confused, Dischord adds, with the Youth Brigade from Los Angeles.
years.xp:
Nathan Strejcek had briefly taken over running Dischord after the Teen Idles ended. According to Wikipedia, Jeff Nelson and Ian MacKaye were disappointed by how little he put into it and took the label back.

Danny Ingram had only started drumming when the Untouchables lost their drummer and he volunteered, never having played before.

years.h: Youth Brigade settle on Bert Queiroz and Tom Clinton
years.p: [[John Falls|44fd383a-ff3f-4028-8cc9-b01b71f5b2dc]] plays guitar for a while and a bassist remembered only as Greg passes through. Youth Brigade settle on [[Bert Queiroz|d657171b-961c-4078-ab84-90b2c69f0095]], Danny Ingram's old Untouchables bandmate, on bass and Tom Clinton on guitar.

eras.title: Nine months, eleven songs
eras.text: Youth Brigade's whole life fits inside 1981: first show in March, last show in December. In between they opened for Black Flag, cut a tour short when guitarist Tom Clinton's mother took back her van, and recorded the songs that became the Possible EP, Dischord No. 6.

years.h: Youth Brigade's first show: Food for Thought
years.p: Youth Brigade debut at Food for Thought, the Dupont Circle restaurant that doubled as a D.C. punk room. Dischord dates it March 1981.

years.h: Youth Brigade open for [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]] at the 9:30 club
years.p: On Black Flag's first trip to the East Coast, Youth Brigade and [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] open at the 9:30 club. Wikipedia credits Youth Brigade with hosting Black Flag's first East Coast show.

years.h: Youth Brigade's tour ends when Tom Clinton's mom wants her van back
years.p: Youth Brigade set out on the road with Minor Threat. According to Wikipedia, the tour ends early when guitarist Tom Clinton's mother, who owns the van, demands it back.
Dischord's dates for Youth Brigade end in December 1981, nine months after the first show at Food for Thought.

q: It sounded so distinct and brave.
years.p: Eight songs in under ten minutes, released as Youth Brigade ends. The title is a joke: one of Dischord's first ads listed a "Possible EP" by Youth Brigade among future releases.
years.xp:
Maximum Rocknroll heard a chunkier, slightly slower thrash than [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]]. The closing track on Possible, No Song II, lasts one second.

Years later Michael Bishop of [[Gwar|f7ccd53a-234c-4800-8d1b-21b201bad1de]] called Barbed Wire crucial, pointing to its sound, drowning in delay and reverb.

eras.title: Filed under Dischord history
eras.text: Youth Brigade was gone before most of D.C. heard it. Dischord kept the songs in circulation, first on the sampler Flex Your Head, then on Four Old 7"s on a 12", which saved the early singles from collector prices.

years.h: Three Youth Brigade songs on Flex Your Head
years.p: Moral Majority, Waste of Time and Last Word land on Dischord's scene sampler. With the Possible EP, Dischord counts 11 Youth Brigade songs released in the band's lifetime.

years.h: Youth Brigade members move on to Rain, Dot Dash and more
years.p: Bert Queiroz goes on to [[Rain|4e9323df-ca77-4e43-addf-bb520fb1b983]] and [[The Meatmen|312c14d9-7897-4608-944a-c5b1c76ae682]]; Danny Ingram to [[Strange Boutique|0ee0668b-fa1d-4db1-ac8c-43a3ad1272c0]], [[Dot Dash|fce03e2d-8138-4418-b29e-499f61c6800e]] and, per Wikipedia, [[Swervedriver|fa6c7999-ff65-486b-9e18-bcb59d6db2f0]]. Nathan Strejcek steps away from the scene.
years.xp: Queiroz also played in Double-O and Second Wind, and Ingram in Emmapeel.

years.p: Dischord gathers Youth Brigade's Possible EP with the early singles by [[The Teen Idles|84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa]], [[SOA|e54cb250-3502-4c32-9482-70488bd9a8cb]] and [[Government Issue|9b952ee8-d45d-4a26-8066-57849d871e06]] on Four Old 7"s on a 12", in print long after the originals vanished.

eras.title: Brigade, reassembled
eras.text: Three decades on, the Salad Days documentary about the D.C. scene needed money, and Nathan Strejcek, Danny Ingram and Bert Queiroz came back to help. Then Dischord finally released the summer 1981 session as Complete First Demo.

years.cap: Youth Brigade at the 9:30 Club, 1982 · Wikimedia
years.h: Youth Brigade reunite at the Black Cat for Salad Days
years.p: Nathan Strejcek, Danny Ingram and Bert Queiroz reunite at the Black Cat for a benefit for the Salad Days documentary. On guitar: [[Steve Hansgen|cd469927-13a8-4d0b-8898-01c6856f5878]], ex-[[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] and [[Government Issue|9b952ee8-d45d-4a26-8066-57849d871e06]].

years.h: Youth Brigade play the 9:30 Club's Punk-Funk Throwdown
years.p: The reunited Youth Brigade, with Steve Hansgen on guitar, play the 9:30 Club as part of its Punk-Funk Throwdown series.
Out of the scene for decades, former Youth Brigade singer Nathan Strejcek co-founds the Delarcos. According to Wikipedia, they release Irradiate in 2023.

years.h: Youth Brigade's first session, out 34 years later
years.p: Youth Brigade recorded eight tracks at Inner Ear in summer 1981 with [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] and [[Skip Groff|8c4d8d50-a6a7-4fa6-9524-6e9c595816c1]]. Most stayed unreleased until Dischord put out Complete First Demo in 2015.
years.xp: Dischord's release notes sum up Youth Brigade in one line: a little over a year, 11 songs released between the Possible EP and Flex Your Head. Complete First Demo was the rest of that first session, pressed on yellow vinyl.
play: It's About Time That We Had a Change

sources.title: Dischord: Complete First Demo out November 23
